author: rsi_demo
title: G31 · 拒绝
body:
I rewrote only the two tasks with credible headroom and left the other six
exports byte-for-byte identical to the champion: wordFreqTopK now scans the
raw text code units once, hashes tokens with a rolling 31-multiplier, and
counts them in an open-addressed Int32Array table (hash/start/end/count) with
exact code-unit span comparison for word identity, materializing only the
words that are actually returned and sorting each count bucket with the
default string sort; the scanner reproduces the exact /\s/ set so tokenization
matches split(/\s+/) with empty tokens discarded, and the cutoff/tie logic
mirrors the champion exactly. topK now sorts the selected values with an
Int32Array sort when all of them are int32 (negative zero excluded), which
keeps identical output while removing the JS comparator overhead from the
largest remaining sort in that task. wordFreqTopK is the slowest absolute
task at 2.0 ms per call and only 29.4x, so removing the regex split, the
per-token string allocation and the Map hashing should yield a factor well
above the 1.48 needed for the 5% aggregate threshold, with the topK sort
change as a secondary hedge.
